newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE releases 1996 report and accounts.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE releases 1996 report and accounts.

text.p: London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Friday its director's report and accounts for 1996, together with the chairman's statement had been approved at the Annual General Meeting held on May 22.

"1996 was LIFFE's busiest year ever," said Chairman Jack Wrigglesworth in his statement in the annual report and accounts. "Records tumbled as we confirmed our position as Europe's number one futures and options exchange and challenged for world leadership in terms of trading volumes."

A record 168 million futures and options contracts, were traded in 1996, an increase of 27 percent on 1995 and 10 percent higher than the exchange's previous busiest year, 1994, LIFFE said in a statement.

LIFFE said the financial surplus had enabled it to make further additions to its reserves, and allowed the board to grant a 39.6 million stg rebate on fee based revenues to its members. The retained surplus after taxation amounted to 19.7 million stg.
Looking to the future, Wrigglesworth said LIFFE was prepared for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) even though it was not yet definite that the process would go ahead.
"Whether or not EMU starts on time, LIFFE will continue to look to the future and anticipate the needs of the markets," he said.

"Good progress was made in 1996 to ensure that LIFFE will enter the next millennium still as the leading international derivatives exchange playing our part to maintain London's position as the preferred and pre-eminent centre for international financial trading activities," Wrigglesworth said. --International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 4041
